title: Beautiful AI artwork needs an open-source path into playable game assets. Who is building it?
author: yaxir
selftext:
AI image generators can produce character artwork that makes me want to build an entire game around it. What I am looking for is a reliable way to turn that artwork into something I can actually control, animate and keep developing.

I am making a 2D action game with dense, detailed arcade pixel graphics. The attached image shows the visual direction: expressive faces, detailed clothing, strong silhouettes and rich shading. I do not have a dedicated artist or animator, so I rely heavily on AI assistance and scripting.

The goal is to take an approved design and build a **reusable, editable character** from it. I want to create running, crouching, jumping, shooting and other actions while preserving the same face, proportions, costume and weapon grip. If an elbow bends badly or a sleeve exposes a gap, I want controls and retained artwork that let me fix it.

Starting material could be a single generated image, a character kit or a sprite sheet. The useful end result would include:

- **Editable construction:** separated parts, completed hidden surfaces, rigs or suitable deformation controls.
- **Reusable animation:** new actions and corrections made from the saved character, with convincing joints, clothing and held objects.
- **Consistent output:** stable pixel scale, palette, transparency, placement and timing across the animation.
- **A documented process:** source files, scripts, worked examples and honest explanations of the remaining manual work.

My priority is 2D, but 2.5D and 3D methods are welcome. A faithful rigged model rendered into sprites could be useful, as could a well-constructed 2D or hybrid character. The final appearance and quality of movement matter most.

I would love to see more **free, open-source frameworks and repositories** connecting these stages, with accessible controls for humans and AI coding agents. Paid generation steps, where present, should be clearly identified and optional where possible.

I think this deserves to be a major direction for AI-assisted game development: giving people lasting control over the assets they generate. A beautiful image should be the beginning of an asset we can keep building on.

**Which existing projects come closest?** Examples showing original artwork → editable source → several finished actions would be especially valuable. And where are the biggest missing pieces that an open-source effort could realistically address?

comments.author: Ill-Past4609
comments.body: You can get your AI to rig it for you just create the editor

comments.author: FragmentedHeap
comments.body:
Everything exists already and is already open sourced.

But it's AI heavy, even locally, do you understand the amount of hardware you will need to run it?

The one I'm building needs the following to run

Main Work Machine:  
\* CPU: 9950x3d  
\* Ram: 2x48 for 192gb ddr5 (like $7000 right now)  
\* GPU: 4090 ($3000+ used)  
\* GPU Number 2: 3090 TI ($1500+ used)  
\* Drives: 3 \* 4 TB NVME (about $1200 each)

Machine Number 2 (LLM inference machine)  
\* CPU 7950x  
\* RAM: 4 \* 32gb (128gb) ddr5  
\* GPU: AMD AI R9700 32GB 

Machine #1 runs dual ComfyUI workloads on both GPUS, and uses the IGPU for the monitor

Machine #2 runs Qwen 3.8 Flash Next on Strata

The software is a docker swarm that runs on the main desktop pc, but also strata on machine #2, it needs all of this just to function.

Image inference is done on the 3090 TI and heavier stuff is on the 4090, and the local LLM's run on the r9700.

Running opensource AI takes a lot of hardware.  I don't think people have $40k to invest in their PC...

comments.body: There are plenty of opensource things already. They are partially on par with tripo for exmaple.

replies.author: ontagi
replies.body: Don't remember all of them by name but there are quite a lot. TRELLIS.2, UltraTex and StableProjectorz are some for a starting point. There also was a decent one for 3d mesh generation for sure, similar to trippo and meshy but I don't remember.

replies.author: FragmentedHeap
replies.body:
ComfyUI has 10000000 plugins for doing this, if you have the hardware to run open source AI/Models, and it has an MCP server you can plug into claude or codex.

There's no such thing as a system that doesn't need ridiculous local hardware though.

Professional 3d designers typically work on maxed out thread ripper builds that cost $50k+  And running local AI is the worst version of that need, it eats tons of hardware.

Either you have a cheap $800 gpu that takes 4 days to render something, or you have a $3000+ gpu that can do it in 2-4 hours.

Or you have a maxed out threadripper with dual rtx 6000 pros that can do them in 4-5 minutes.

replies.author: ImpressiveGooseHead
replies.body:
OP please don’t listen to this person. I have no idea where they’re getting their info from. I’ve been working professionally as a cg artist at the biggest, fanciest studios for decades, and nobody’s ever been on a 50k machine.

As a point of reference, I run trellis and other comfy ui workflows on a 3090 plus 64gb ram for character models without issue. You generally break into pieces for better quality, and then sculpt from there.

And this is for realtime cinematic quality metahuman work. For anything more just send to the cloud for final pass.

replies.author: FragmentedHeap
replies.body:
$50k if you want to make a TON of crap really really fast.

Todays prices

A 3090 used is $1700 right now, and 64 gb of ddr5 memory is $940 at the min, cpu $500+, a 4tb ssd is $1300+. Easily $4500+ for the most basic PC for doing this.

And that's at todays prices.

With todays RAM prices that 50k machine is what used to be $8k.... just 2 years ago.

Good luck even finding a 3090 right now, $2000+ in most places.  4090 going for $3k, and a 5090 is $8000+ right now.

Mac Book Pro, $6500+, Mac Studio, $7500+

You will be hard pressed to find hardware right now for less than $4500 (on a good day, all in).

If you built my 9950x3d with 192gb ram and 1 4090 right now at todays prices, it would cost you $20k, even though I paid about $5k all in.

The consumer market is absolutely screwed right now.
